model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)
model_label: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (run on the component engine: revenue x FFO margin, less the FFO-to-FAD bridge (2nd-generation TI/leasing commissions, maintenance capex, straight-line and other non-cash items) = FAD, BXP's own Nareit-plus AFFO-equivalent; net debt NOT deducted because FAD is already after net interest expense)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 (Dec-25 year) total revenue, US$m, from BXP_Metrics.csv core_metrics (10-K FY2025). Revenue is the DRIVER line only; the flow valued is FAD (Funds Available for Distribution), BXP's own non-GAAP measure that starts from FFO and deducts 2nd-generation tenant improvements/leasing commissions, maintenance capex, hotel improvements and non-cash straight-line/hedge items -- i.e. AFFO as BXP defines it. FY2025 FFO margin on revenue was 31.3%; FAD margin was 21.6%.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average common and common-equivalent shares, Q2 2026 (159,629 thousand; Q2 2026 press-release FFO reconciliation, 8-K filed 2026-07-28). Basic shares outstanding at 30-Jun-2026 were 159,521,510 (10-Q balance sheet). Held FLAT: no material buyback program active (BXP has been a net share issuer historically via DRIP/ATM, offset by dividend cut reducing the need for equity issuance); SBC is expensed inside FFO/FAD via the stock-based-compensation add-back/deduct in the FAD bridge, so charging further dilution would double count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow discounted is FAD, which is already AFTER net interest expense (interest expense is deducted before FFO in the consolidated income statement, and FFO in turn nets to net income which already reflects it). Deducting the balance-sheet net debt on top would charge financing cost twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never capitalise a post-interest flow and then subtract net debt). total_debt and cash below are recorded for audit/leverage-context only.
inputs.total_debt_note: US$m at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q/press-release balance sheet): mortgage notes payable, net 4,281.2 + unsecured senior notes, net 8,811.2 + unsecured exchangeable senior notes, net 978.6 + unsecured line of credit 0.0 + unsecured term loans, net 797.6 + unsecured commercial paper 750.0 = 15,618.6. Excludes finance/operating lease liabilities (353.4 + 386.5), consistent with the Metrics.csv TotalDebt correction basis. This is materially higher than the FY2024 CSV figure (16,220.5 at 31-Dec-2024) net of the ~$600m paid down since, before the $700m 6.05% notes due 2036 were issued in Aug-2026 to refinance $1bn of 2.75% notes maturing Oct-2026 (net effect on the balance already reflected in the 6/30/2026 figures above, which predate the Aug-2026 refinancing settlement).
inputs.cash_note: US$m at 30-Jun-2026 (10-Q balance sheet). Down sharply from $1,478.2m at 31-Dec-2025 -- BXP drew down cash in H1 2026 (debt paydown / development funding ahead of the Aug-2026 notes issuance). Recorded for audit only; not netted against the FAD-capitalised value.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 FAD (Funds Available for Distribution to common shareholders and common unitholders), US$m, reconstructed by summing the four quarterly FAD reconciliations disclosed in BXP's quarterly supplemental packages (Q1 2025 213.885 + Q2 2025 203.592 + Q3 2025 201.772 + Q4 2025 134.515 = 753.764). This is the flow the valuation capitalises. NOT the CSV FreeCashFlow of 5.912 (OCF 1,245.157 less ALL capex 1,239.245, which includes growth/development capex on new life-science and residential projects, not just the maintenance/leasing capex FAD deducts) and NOT reported FFO of 1,089.072 (FFO is pre the TI/leasing-commission and maintenance-capex bridge; capitalising FFO directly would overstate the distributable flow by ignoring recurring re-leasing capital intensity, which is unusually high for this portfolio given active repositioning in SF/Seattle/DC).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 FFO (Funds From Operations, Nareit definition) attributable to BXP, Inc., US$m, reconstructed from quarterly diluted FFO per share x diluted weighted-average shares (Q1 1.64x158.9=260.6, Q2 1.71x158.8=271.7, Q3 1.74x159.0=276.7, Q4 1.76x159.2=280.2, total 1,089.1m, i.e. $6.85/diluted share). FY2024 FFO was $7.10/share and FY2023 was $7.28/share (both per year-end 8-K press releases) -- FFO/share has DECLINED three years running as net interest expense grew faster than revenue/NOI (pandemic-era low-coupon debt rolling into a much higher-rate environment), before FY2026 guidance of $6.99-$7.05/share (+2-3% at the midpoint) marks the first projected increase.
inputs.sbc_source: Stock-based compensation (US$44.3m FY2025 per Metrics.csv) is expensed inside FFO (deducted from net income before FFO is struck) and is one of the FAD-bridge add-backs (it is added back to FFO within the FAD reconciliation, then not separately deducted as capex): net effect, SBC is already reflected once in the flow being valued and is not added back a second time here. No further SBC adjustment is made; house and street bases coincide (SBC-zero convention, consistent with the REIT row of the routing table).
inputs.interest_income_note: Zero. BXP holds working cash, not a material net-cash position (net debt ~$15.1bn); no interest income is excluded from or added back to the flow.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:02Z NYSE regular close (Yahoo v8 chart meta); 52-week range 49.72-76.37
inputs.nta_note: GAAP book value per BXP Inc. common share: stockholders' equity attributable to BXP, Inc. $5,155.1m / 159.522m shares outstanding = $32.32. Historical-cost book value under real-estate depreciation, NOT a fair-value NTA (BXP does not report investment property at IAS-40 fair value; its real estate is carried at depreciated cost, US$20,991.8m gross less US$8,277.7m accumulated depreciation at 30-Jun-2026). Recorded as a leverage/solvency cross-check only, not a valuation floor -- a depreciated-cost book value understates the economic value of a trophy CBD portfolio and is not comparable to GPT.AX-style fair-value NTA.
inputs.dividend_history_note: Quarterly common dividend cut 29% from $0.98 to $0.70, effective Q3 2025 (announced Sept-2025 alongside a 'strategic reset' at BXP's Triennial Investor Day). FY2025 FAD payout ratio (actual mixed-rate year) was 78.9% (distributions $594.4m / FAD $753.8m); at the new $0.70/qtr run-rate against trailing-twelve-month FAD (Q3'25-Q2'26, $567.0m) the payout ratio is 87.6% ($496.4m / $567.0m) -- FAD cover is thinner on a trailing basis than the FY2025 annual figure because 2nd-generation TI/leasing commissions were unusually front-loaded in Q1 2026 ($178.4m) on strong SF lease commencements (680 Folsom, 50 Hawthorne). Cross-check only; not a model input.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the USD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because FAD is a post-interest flow and no net debt is deducted. 10-year US Treasury ~5.1-5.2% (Sep-2026, ^TNX) + 1.2 beta x 5.5% US equity risk premium = 11.7%, rounded to 11.5%. Beta of 1.2 (above 1.0) reflects office-REIT-specific leverage and rate sensitivity above the broader REIT sector (Analysis JSON rates interest-rate sensitivity 'high' and macro/regional risk 'moderate-high'). The same 11.5% is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once, in the flows, not the rate). Cross-check: at current_price the market capitalises TTM FAD/share of $3.55 at a 5.6% FAD yield and FY2026E FFO/share of $7.02 at an 11.1% FFO yield -- both far above a typical REIT's cost of equity, i.e. the market is pricing continued FAD-cover deterioration and/or a further dividend cut, materially more bearish than this model's base case.
inputs.lease_treatment: BXP's own operating and finance lease liabilities as lessee (ground leases; $386.5m operating + $353.4m finance at 30-Jun-2026) are immaterial relative to the $15.6bn secured/unsecured debt stack and sit inside FFO/FAD as an operating expense; not separately modelled and not included in total_debt above (consistent with the debt figure's own composition, which excludes lease liabilities).
inputs.nci_treatment: FFO and FAD are BOTH already stated net of noncontrolling interests -- both the Operating Partnership common units (~9.8-10% of consolidated FFO in recent quarters, since BXP Inc. owns ~90% of Boston Properties LP) and the larger property-partnership NCI (JV partners' share of consolidated development/JV assets, $2,018.8m of the $7,729.7m total equity at 30-Jun-2026). The per-share FFO and FAD figures used throughout this model are 'attributable to BXP, Inc.' after both NCI deductions, so no further NCI adjustment is made in the bridge (same convention as CHC.AX: flows are attributable-only by construction).
inputs.notes: Model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity -- routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods SKILL.md REIT row (large-cap office/life-science REIT; GAAP net income dominated by impairments/gains on sale in recent years -- FY2025 NI $384.0m, FY2024 NI $84.2m after ~$500m+ of unconsolidated-JV impairments -- so statutory earnings and reported FreeCashFlow, which nets ALL capex including growth development spend, are both set aside). Run on the Drivers/engine route, GPT.AX/CHC.AX precedent: revenue is the driver line, EBITDA margin = FFO margin (post-interest: net income already reflects interest expense before FFO is struck), D&A = 0 (FFO already adds back real-estate D&A, so it is not deducted again downstream), SBC = 0 (expensed inside FFO/FAD, per sbc_source above), capex = the FFO-to-FAD bridge as % of revenue (2nd-gen TI/leasing commissions + maintenance capex + hotel improvements, net of small non-cash add-backs), working capital = 0, net_debt = 0, cash_tax_rate = 0 (BXP qualifies as a REIT and distributes taxable income; no material corporate income tax on the REIT). First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry -- this run adds the first BXP line to MEMORY.md). Price is the 25-Sep-2026 NYSE regular close. Balance sheet, debt and share count are from the 30-Jun-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-06), the latest filing; FFO/FAD quarterly detail is reconstructed from the Q1 2025 through Q2 2026 quarterly earnings-release supplemental packages (8-K exhibits) since BXP.duckdb's core_metrics/kpis tables do not carry FFO/AFFO/FAD (US SEC filer parsed via XBRL, which does not tag REIT non-GAAP supplemental metrics) -- these should be backfilled into kpis on a future refresh so this reconstruction is not required again.

historical_growth.eps_basis: Statutory EPS is not used: FY2023 NI $190.2m/$1.21 EPS, FY2024 NI $14.3m/$0.09 EPS (unconsolidated-JV impairments), FY2025 NI $384.0m -- a sequence of impairments and gains on sale, not operating performance. FFO per diluted share is the relevant series and is NEGATIVE growth over 3 years: FY2023 $7.28 -> FY2024 $7.10 (-2.5%) -> FY2025 $6.85 (-3.5%), a cumulative -5.9% over 2 years (net interest expense has grown faster than NOI as pandemic-era debt refinances at much higher coupons). FY2026 guidance of $6.99-$7.05 (+2.1% at midpoint) is the first projected increase in three years.
historical_growth.fcf_basis: FAD is only reliably reconstructable for FY2025 from quarterly supplementals in this session (BXP does not appear to have consistently disclosed FAD as far back as FY2021-2022 supplementals were not pulled); no FAD CAGR is calculated. Reported CSV FreeCashFlow (OCF less all capex, including growth development spend) swings from -$124.2m (FY2017) to $386.4m (FY2022) to $5.9m (FY2025) purely on the phasing of the development pipeline and is not a meaningful growth series for a capital-intensive developer-REIT (per the Metrics.csv adjudication note).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 FFO guidance (+2.1% at the midpoint on a flat share count) is the anchor for Year 1; the base path assumes modest reacceleration toward 3-3.5% as the life-science/residential development pipeline completes lease-up and the Q2 2026 leasing momentum (129% of the 10-year Q2 average, occupancy +100bp to 88.4%) continues, before fading to 2.5% long-run (roughly CPI/embedded-escalator growth for a mature CBD office portfolio). Equity CAGR is not used as the primary anchor: BXP's book value reflects historical-cost depreciation and JV impairments, not organic growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: FFO/share CAGR (-2.5% to -3.5%/yr over FY2023-25) diverges sharply from revenue CAGR (+3.2% 3yr), by far more than 30%. The divergence is net interest expense growing faster than revenue/NOI as low-coupon pandemic-era debt refinances into a much higher-rate environment (e.g. $700m of 2.75% notes due Oct-2026 refinanced in Aug-2026 with $700m of 6.05% notes due 2036) -- not a decline in underlying property performance. Growth is taken from the reaffirmed/raised FY2026 FFO guidance rather than the trailing revenue or equity series.
historical_growth.notes: This is a REIT in the middle of a structural balance-sheet reset (29% dividend cut Sept-2025, ~$1.0bn+ of non-core dispositions closed with a ~$1.9bn cumulative target by 2028, both aimed at self-funding the life-science/residential development pipeline and delevering) rather than a steady-state compounder. Revenue growth (3.2-4.5%/yr) has been positive throughout, but FFO/share growth has been negative for three straight years purely on the interest-expense line; FAD -- the flow this model actually capitalises -- also carries elevated capex intensity for a portfolio undergoing heavy TI/leasing-commission-funded re-leasing in weak submarkets (SF, Seattle, DC net effective rents down double digits). None of the standard CAGR anchors (equity, EPS, reported FCF) describe this business cleanly; the base case is built off management's own reaffirmed FY2026 guidance instead.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 (2.0%) lands FY2026E FFO/share at ~$7.03, matching the reaffirmed $6.99-$7.05 guidance midpoint on a flat share count. Y2-Y4 (2.8-3.3%) reflect continued flight-to-quality leasing (Q2 2026: 1.8M sq ft leased, 129% of the 10-year average; AI/tech now ~80% of new SF leasing) and lease-up of the life-science/residential pipeline (targeting >12% of ARO) plus embedded contractual rent escalators, offset by negative releasing spreads still working through Seattle/DC/parts of SF. Fades to 2.5% (roughly CPI-linked escalator growth) once the current lease-up wave is absorbed and the disposition program (non-core assets sold, shrinking the base modestly) completes around 2028.
base.margin_rationale: FFO margin (this row is read as FFO/revenue, the flow before the FAD capex bridge) recovers gradually from the FY2025 actual of 31.3% as management's stated FY2026 target of lower net interest expense (disposition proceeds funding debt paydown, partially offset by higher-coupon refinancing such as the Aug-2026 $700m 6.05% notes) takes hold, and as capital-light development/management fee income and life-science lease-up add higher-margin revenue. Held flat at 32.8% in the outer years -- no assumption of a return to the FY2023 34.3% margin, since post-2026-era debt coupons are structurally higher than the pandemic-era book being replaced.
base.capex_rationale: The FFO-to-FAD bridge (2nd-generation TI/leasing commissions, maintenance capex, hotel improvements, net of small non-cash add-backs) held near the FY2025 actual of 9.6% of revenue, easing slightly toward 9.2% as the current heavy re-leasing wave in SF (elevated per-square-foot transaction costs, ~$11.55-11.80/sq ft/year recently) normalizes once occupancy stabilizes above 90%. This is materially below the TTM run-rate bridge of ~15.1% of revenue, which was inflated by an unusually front-loaded Q1 2026 TI/leasing quarter ($178.4m on 2.3M sq ft of commencements); the FY2025 full-year figure is used as the less noisy base. Gives FY2026E FAD of ~$4.90/share versus a TTM actual of $3.55/share -- the base case explicitly assumes the FY2025 annual capital-intensity ratio, not the currently-elevated trailing four quarters, which is the single largest source of uncertainty in this valuation (see key_risks_to_valuation).
base.tax_rationale: Zero: BXP qualifies and elects to be taxed as a REIT and distributes at least 90% of REIT taxable income, eliminating corporate-level income tax on that income; FFO/FAD are already the after-tax distributable flow.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 11.5% / 2.5% = 11.1x terminal FAD (a 9.0% terminal FAD yield) binds below the 16x cap. BXP itself trades at ~17.8x TTM FAD/share today, but that trailing multiple is depressed by the temporarily elevated TI/leasing bridge described above; on the FY2025 annual FAD basis the current multiple is closer to 13.5x.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2026 beats guidance as Q2 2026 did ($0.08/share above midpoint); the AI/tech-driven San Francisco leasing wave broadens to other gateway markets, the life-science pipeline leases up faster than planned, and the Fed cuts rates through 2027 easing both net interest expense growth and cap-rate pressure. Disposition proceeds are redeployed into higher-return CBD development rather than pure debt paydown, supporting above-guidance FFO growth for several years before fading to a still-healthy 3.0%.
bull.margin_rationale: FFO margin recovers toward the FY2023 level (34.3%) as lower rates ease refinancing pressure faster than the base case assumes and occupancy gains (portfolio occupancy above 88.4% and rising) drive operating leverage on largely fixed property-level costs.
bull.capex_rationale: TI/leasing-commission intensity eases as the current heavy re-leasing wave completes and rolls into a more normalized, lower-incentive leasing environment once flight-to-quality absorption tightens available trophy supply further.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 11.5% / 3.0% = 11.8x, still inside the 16x cap. Same 11.5% cost of equity as base: the bull case is better flows and margin recovery, not a cheaper discount rate.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 lands a point under the low end of guidance as one or more of the Sumner Square-style impairment/disposition surprises recur. The structural, not cyclical, decline in aggregate office demand reasserts itself: negative releasing spreads deepen in San Francisco (-17.8%), Seattle (-20.1%) and DC (-10.2%), the life-science pipeline's lease-up stalls on continued biotech funding softness, and portfolio occupancy stalls or slips below 88%. Growth troughs slightly negative in Y2 before a slow recovery to 1.5%, below CPI, as the disposition program shrinks the earning asset base faster than new leasing replaces it.
bear.margin_rationale: FFO margin keeps compressing as more pandemic-era low-coupon debt rolls into materially higher rates (the 2.75%-to-6.05% refinancing pattern repeats on further maturities) faster than NOI growth or disposition-funded deleveraging can offset, and DC federal-workforce-related demand softness pressures that submarket further.
bear.capex_rationale: TI/leasing-commission intensity rises as tenants demand larger concessions to commit in a weakening office market (mirroring the elevated TTM bridge already observed at ~15% of revenue), pushing FAD cover of even the reset $0.70/qtr distribution toward or below 1.0x by the outer years, raising the risk of a second dividend cut (flagged as a financial risk in the Analysis JSON).
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 11.5% / 1.5% = 10.0x binds just under the 12x cap (a 10.0% exit FAD yield, consistent with distressed office-REIT pricing seen in 2023-2024).

scenario_narratives.base: BXP delivers the reaffirmed FY2026 FFO guidance ($6.99-$7.05/share) as flight-to-quality leasing (AI/tech now ~80% of new San Francisco demand, Q2 2026 leasing at 129% of the 10-year average) offsets continued negative releasing spreads in Seattle, DC and parts of San Francisco, and the life-science/residential pipeline gradually lifts occupancy from 88.4%. FFO margin recovers modestly from the FY2025 trough (31.3%) as disposition-funded debt paydown partly offsets higher-coupon refinancing. The FFO-to-FAD bridge -- currently elevated on a trailing basis by a lumpy, front-loaded TI/leasing quarter -- normalizes toward the FY2025 annual ratio (9.6% of revenue), leaving FAD cover of the reset $0.70/qtr distribution comfortably above 1.0x. No cap-rate compression or discount-rate relief is assumed: FAD is capitalised at an 11.5% USD cost of equity, well above the ~5.6% FAD yield / ~11.1% FFO yield the current price implies, i.e. the market is pricing continued FAD-cover deterioration that this base case does not assume.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Q2 2026 guidance-beat pattern continues, the AI/tech-driven San Francisco leasing wave broadens to Boston, New York and eventually DC/Seattle, the life-science pipeline leases up ahead of schedule, and Fed rate cuts through 2027 ease both net interest expense growth and the cost of refinancing maturing low-coupon debt. FFO margin recovers toward the FY2023 level (34.3%) as occupancy gains create operating leverage, TI/leasing-commission intensity normalizes as trophy-asset scarcity tightens, and disposition proceeds fund accretive CBD/life-science development rather than pure deleveraging. FFO grows 3-4.5% for several years before fading to a still-healthy 3.0% long-run rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: The structural decline in aggregate US office demand from hybrid work reasserts itself even for BXP's trophy assets: negative releasing spreads deepen across San Francisco, Seattle and DC, the life-science pipeline's lease-up stalls on continued biotech funding softness, and portfolio occupancy slips back below 88%. Pandemic-era low-coupon debt keeps rolling into materially higher rates (mirroring the $700m 2.75%-to-6.05% refinancing already completed), compressing FFO margin toward 28% by the outer years. TI/leasing-commission intensity rises as tenants extract larger concessions in a weaker market, pushing FAD cover of even the already-reset $0.70/qtr distribution toward 1.0x and raising real risk of a second dividend cut. Exit at a 10x FAD multiple, consistent with 2023-2024 distressed office-REIT pricing.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted above the house default (15%) to 30%: the Analysis JSON rates structural office demand headwinds, refinancing risk and interest-rate sensitivity all 'high', BXP already cut its dividend once (Sept-2025, -29%) which is itself evidence the prior payout was not comfortably covered, FFO/share has declined for three consecutive years, and the market's own implied FFO/FAD yields (11.1%/5.6%) are already pricing something closer to this bear case than the base case. Base cut to 45% (from the house default 50%) to make room for the elevated bear weight; the reaffirmed-and-raised FY2026 guidance and genuinely strong Q2 2026 leasing/occupancy momentum (129% of 10-year average, AI/tech absorption in SF) still make it the single most likely outcome. Bull held at 25%: real and observable (not speculative) momentum exists, but sustained multi-year outperformance requires several things to go right simultaneously (rate cuts, broadening flight-to-quality demand, life-science recovery, no further impairments).

valuation_philosophy.summary: BXP is valued as a stream of FAD (Funds Available for Distribution -- FFO less 2nd-generation tenant-improvement/leasing-commission capex, maintenance capex and other recurring re-leasing costs) capitalised at an 11.5% USD cost of equity, with no net-debt deduction because FAD is already after the company's ~$700-900m/yr of net interest expense. Statutory net income (dominated by unconsolidated-JV impairments and gains on sale -- FY2024 NI of just $14.3m against $1.1bn of FFO) and reported free cash flow (which nets ALL capex, including growth development spend on the life-science/residential pipeline) are both set aside as unrepresentative of distributable earning power. The base case is essentially the reaffirmed FY2026 FFO guidance with the FFO-to-FAD bridge normalized to its FY2025 annual ratio (not the currently noisy, front-loaded trailing-twelve-month ratio), fading to a CPI-like 2.5% long-run growth rate. Historical-cost book value ($32.32/share) is recorded as a leverage cross-check only, not a valuation floor, since BXP does not carry investment property at fair value the way an IAS-40 REIT does. At the current price the market is capitalising TTM FAD/share at a 5.6% yield and FY2026E FFO/share at an 11.1% yield -- both suggesting the market is pricing continued FAD-cover deterioration and/or a second dividend cut, a materially more bearish view than this model's probability-weighted base case, which is itself already tilted toward bear (30% weight) given three consecutive years of FFO/share decline and one dividend cut already delivered.
key_risks_to_valuation: The FFO-to-FAD bridge (TI/leasing commissions + maintenance capex) is the single largest source of model uncertainty: the base case uses the FY2025 annual ratio (9.6% of revenue) rather than the currently elevated trailing-twelve-month ratio (~15%), and if the higher trailing intensity persists rather than normalizing, FAD and the resulting valuation fall materially -- this is exactly the bear case's axis.

Refinancing risk: pandemic-era low-coupon debt (e.g. $700m of 2.75% notes) continues rolling into materially higher rates (6.05% on the Aug-2026 replacement notes), and FFO margin has already compressed from 34.3% (FY2023) to 31.3% (FY2025) on this dynamic alone.

Dividend coverage: the September 2025 cut to $0.70/quarter (-29%) was itself evidence the prior payout was not comfortably covered; trailing FAD payout is already 87.6%, and a second cut is a live risk if TI/leasing intensity does not normalize.

Structural office demand: even BXP's trophy/flight-to-quality assets face negative releasing spreads in San Francisco, Seattle and DC; life-science, previously a growth driver, has softened industry-wide on reduced biotech funding.

Discount rate: every 50bp on the 11.5% cost of equity moves the base value materially given the long terminal-value tail typical of a capitalisation model; the current price already implies a far higher (~11%+ FFO yield) required return than the house rate.

Revenue is the driver line, not the valued flow: a shift in FFO margin (net interest expense trajectory, disposition-driven asset-base shrinkage) can move the outcome without any change in revenue growth.
